newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill two in troubled Pakistani city.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill two in troubled Pakistani city.

text.p: Gunmen shot and killed two people in Pakistan's troubled city of Karachi on Thursday, bringing the death toll from ethnic and sectarian violence to 13 in the past three days, police and witnesses said.
A 40-year-old man was shot dead in the Federal B Area of District Central. In a separate attack masked gunmen killed a 60-year-old man at his home in the Malir district, police said.
There was no immediate word on the political affiliations of the victims or on the motives for the attacks.
In a separate incident, armed men commandeered an ambulance of the private Edhi Welfare Trust, police said.

Witnesses said gunmen apparently loyal to the breakaway Haqiqi faction of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) forced shops to close in at least six Karachi districts. They burned three vehicles and blocked traffic.
The MQM-Haqiqi activists were protesting against Tuesday's attack on their headquarters in which gunmen killed two party workers.
MQM-Haqiqi leader Afaq Ahmed blamed the government, rather than the mainstream MQM, for the assault. Karachi police chief Malik Mohammad Iqbal rejected the accusation.
The MQM, now part of the Sindh province coalition government, has long feuded with the MQM-Haqiqi faction.
This week's shootings have sparked fears that this year's relative lull in violence in Karachi may be coming to an end.
More than 50 people have been killed in ethnic, political and sectarian unrest in Karachi this year, compared to 500 last year and about 2,000 in 1995.
